item.title: Europe stocks rise as oil retreat aids sentiment; PMI data in focus
item.description: European shares inched higher on Wednesday as lower oil prices supported sentiment, while investors awaited key business activity data due later in the day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: European shares inched higher on Wednesday as lower oil prices supported sentiment, while investors awaited key business activity data due later in the day. The benchmark pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) was up 0.4% at 645.04 points by 0708 GMT. Most major regional bourses also traded higher. Investors awaited S&P Global's flash September purchasing managers' index (PMI) survey for the euro zone, which could provide fresh clues on the health of the region's economy. Aerospace and defence stocks (.SXPARO) led sectoral gains, with Saab (SAABb.ST) and Exosens (EXENS.PA) among the top performers. Oil prices extended their decline as investors assessed the prospect of increased Gulf supplies after Saudi Arabia restarted operations at a key pipeline. Energy stocks (.SXEP) , however, rose 0.8%. Among individual stocks, KWS (KWSG.DE) shed 6.1% after the German seed producer's annual net sales fell 3% to €1.63 billion ($1.86 billion), missing IBES estimate of €1.68 bln, hit by lower sugarbeet and corn acreage. Shares of Adyen (ADYEN.AS) slipped roughly 2% after the Dutch payments processor named Klarna's (KLAR.N) Niclas Neglen as its next chief financial officer, effective February 1, 2027.

item.title: Weak monsoon curbs farm-input demand in India, Rallis India CEO says
item.description: India's weak monsoon is prompting farmers to cut spending on pesticides, fertilisers and seeds this year, the chief executive of Tata Chemicals unit Rallis India said.
item.dc:creator: Surbhi Misra
item.content:encoded: India's weak monsoon is prompting farmers to cut spending on pesticides, fertilisers and seeds this year, the chief executive of Tata Chemicals (TTCH.NS) unit Rallis India (RALL.NS) said. The June-September monsoon, which accounts for nearly 70% of the country's annual rainfall, has been erratic this year and remains [USN:P8N43102P TEXT:"well below normal"], raising concerns about crop yields, rural incomes and food inflation in Asia's No.3 economy. Monsoon rainfall was 15% below the average, as of September 21, Barclays said this week, adding that rainfall was 18% below normal so far in September and 16% below normal in August. "When rainfall certainty is very low, farmers tend to save on resources," agrochemicals and seeds firm Rallis India Managing Director and CEO Gyanendra Shukla said in an interview earlier this week. "Farmers are not very certain of full harvest as they would have anticipated." Indian farmers typically sow summer crops such as rice, soybeans and cotton from June as monsoon rains arrive, while winter crops including wheat and rapeseed are planted from October after the monsoon retreats. "There will be compression in the overall use of crop protection products, fertilisers and seed," Shukla said, highlighting how demand for herbicides and fungicides had been particularly weak. Rallis peers Dhanuka Agritech (DHNP.NS) and Godrej Agrovet (GODE.NS) have also blamed erratic monsoon rains for weak demand for crop-protection products. India's farm input sector is also ripe for consolidation, Shukla said, arguing that low barriers to entry had led to an overcrowded market. "There are too many players," he said, adding that companies focused on innovation and strong partnerships would be best positioned to withstand intensifying competition.

item.title: Reijnders says Man City role, Saudi offer prompted surprise summer switch
item.description: Netherlands midfielder Tijjani Reijnders said he did not like the role he was being asked to play at Manchester City and that he could not turn down the financial package being offered by Saudi Arabia's Al Qadsiah.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Netherlands midfielder Tijjani Reijnders said he did not like the role he was being asked to play at Manchester City and that he could not turn down the financial package being offered by Saudi Arabia's Al Qadsiah. Reijnders, who joined the Saudi Pro League side in a surprise 61 million euro ($69.70 million) move, had wanted to play as a dynamic midfielder, moving between attack and defence, but increasingly found himself playing more as an attacking midfielder. "In pre-season, I noticed that things were heading in that direction again at City, and I started thinking about whether I wanted another season like that,” he told reporters as the Dutch national team prepared for Thursday’s Nations League game against Germany. “The honest answer was no. I wanted to look elsewhere, and then I heard from the club that I was allowed to do so. "I think a lot of people have the idea that your career as a top footballer is over when you make a move like this. I initially felt that way too," he said of the Saudi switch. Discussions with Al Qadsiah coach Brendan Rodgers convinced him otherwise. "He said I could have three or four very enjoyable years here and then return to Europe. There are enough examples of that now. That is my goal too," Reijnders, 28, said. "With all the big names, I actually rate the Saudi league higher than the Eredivisie (Dutch league). If people want to judge the football there, they should watch it first." Reports said Reijnders had signed a deal worth around 100 million euros over four years in Saudi Arabia. "You can always play the moralist, but I think everyone would say yes to that," he said. "I don't want to have to work anymore after my career. I didn't need to after City either, but now I can also set up future generations of my family well. "If this choice means my grandchildren can also live comfortably, why wouldn't I do it?" ($1 = 0.8751 euros)

item.title: France private sector returns to growth at fastest rate in 25 months, PMI shows
item.description: France's private sector grew in September at its fastest pace in just over two years, driven by a rebound in services demand, a business survey showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France's private sector grew in September at its fastest pace in just over two years, driven by a rebound in services demand, a business survey showed on Wednesday. The S&P Global Flash France Composite Output Index, a preliminary estimate, rose to 51.2 from 48.5 in August, a survey by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction. "The French economy displayed surprising resilience in September, although the durability of this expansion is questionable given new orders barely rose and firms' own expectations for activity deteriorated," said Joe Hayes, Senior Principal Economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. Services provided most of the momentum. The Flash France Services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 51.4 from 48.0, a 10-month high, while manufacturing output growth slowed and remained only marginal. Demand improved only mildly. New orders rose for the first time in 10 months, while new foreign business posted its softest contraction of the year-to-date, helping drive the quickest increase in outstanding business volumes in almost three-and-a-half years. Companies still cut staff for a fifth successive month, with respondents citing redundancies, resignations and non-renewal of temporary contracts. At the same time, input costs and output charges both rose at their fastest rates since May, fuelled by higher fuel, energy, metals and component prices. Still, business expectations worsened again, leaving French companies the least optimistic about the year-ahead outlook since May as higher interest rates, political uncertainty and international competition weighed on confidence.

item.title: Tom Cruise se desata con su personaje de "Digger" en un estreno repleto de estrellas
item.description: Tom Cruise describió a su personaje en "Digger" como "completamente escandaloso" y diferente a cualquier papel que hubiera interpretado antes durante el estreno mundial de la película en Londres el martes.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Halliwell
item.content:encoded: Tom Cruise describió a su personaje en "Digger" como "completamente escandaloso" y diferente a cualquier papel que hubiera interpretado antes durante el estreno mundial de la película en Londres el martes. "Es el tipo de personaje que dice cosas que algunas personas piensan, pero que otras ni siquiera se atreven a imaginar", dijo la estrella de Hollywood a Reuters. "Nunca había leído un personaje ni un guion como estos". El estreno de "Digger" se celebró con una gala a la que asistieron el príncipe Guillermo y la princesa Catalina de Inglaterra, tras lo que la actriz Sandra Hüller describió como casi diez años de trabajo del director ganador de un Óscar, Alejandro González Iñárritu. La película ha generado mucha expectación desde que se publicó un tráiler en el que se veía a Cruise transformado en el excéntrico magnate petrolero Digger Rockwell, con el pelo canoso, prótesis faciales y un traje acolchado. Cruise dijo que esta transformación distaba mucho de ser el aspecto más exigente del papel, y señaló en su lugar un monólogo de 10 minutos rodado en una sola toma. Hüller, protagonista de "Anatomía de una caída", dijo que fue "extraordinario" ver la interpretación de Cruise. "Da la sensación de que todo lo que ha aprendido en 46 años de carrera como actor ha confluido en este personaje", añadió. En la película, Rockwell provoca sin querer un desastre ecológico que lleva al mundo al borde de una guerra nuclear, antes de apresurarse a salvar el planeta. Sin embargo, los creadores de la película han revelado muy poco más sobre la historia, lo que ha alimentado las especulaciones sobre la trama y los rumores de que podría tratarse de un musical, algo que Cruise ha desmentido. "Si ves la película sin saber nada de ella, es mucho mejor que si ya lo supieras de antemano", afirmó Hüller, quien añadió que el secretismo no tenía como objetivo crear intriga por el simple hecho de hacerlo. Mientras que Cruise describió la historia como una exploración del "poder y la codicia (…), la responsabilidad y la irresponsabilidad", la actriz australiana Sophie Wilde señaló que también transmitía un mensaje sobre el arte como "un vehículo para la catarsis". Iñárritu, entre cuyos trabajos anteriores se cuentan "Birdman" y "El renacido", comparó el proceso de creación de "Digger" con la pintura, y señaló que cada fotograma se había elaborado con esmero para sumergir al público en el mundo de la película. Para Emma D’Arcy, esa atención al detalle hizo que trabajar con el cineasta mexicano fuera como formar parte de una orquesta dirigida por un director. "En 'Digger', la musicalidad era realmente muy, muy importante (…). Es una comedia, así que el ritmo es fundamental". Michael Stuhlbarg, protagonista de "Call Me by Your Name" ("Llámame por tu nombre" en algunos países hispanohablantes), recordó que las escenas evolucionaban constantemente durante el rodaje, con nuevos diálogos, versiones alternativas y añadidos inesperados que surgían de un día para otro. El actor bromeó diciendo que se rodó tanto material inusual que espera que algún día se lance un DVD con metraje adicional de la producción. "Nos lo pasamos muy bien", dijo. "Digger" comenzará su estreno mundial en cines el 30 de septiembre y se estrenará en las salas de Estados Unidos y Reino Unido el 2 de octubre.

item.title: México detiene a un supuesto líder del tráfico de fentanilo con apoyo de EEUU
item.description: Un presunto narcotraficante mexicano, acusado de coordinar y financiar una organización dedicada al transporte de precursores químicos utilizados para la producción de fentanilo desde China hacia México y Estados Unidos, fue detenido el martes en Ciudad de México, según informó el ministro de Seguridad de México.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un presunto narcotraficante mexicano, acusado de coordinar y financiar una organización dedicada al transporte de precursores químicos utilizados para la producción de fentanilo desde China hacia México y Estados Unidos, fue detenido el martes en Ciudad de México, según informó el ministro de Seguridad de México. José Ángel Rivera, también conocido por su alias "Don Flaco", fue detenido por las autoridades mexicanas en una operación conjunta llevada a cabo junto con el FBI y la Agencia Antidroga de Estados Unidos (DEA), según indicó Omar García Harfuch en una publicación en X. Rivera había sido sancionado por el Departamento de Estado de EEUU en enero de 2023 por su presunta implicación en el tráfico de fentanilo hacia Estados Unidos. "Con cooperación internacional, responsabilidad compartida y respeto irrestricto a nuestra soberanía cerramos el paso al dinero que financia a las organizaciones criminales que tanto daño hacen en México y en otros países", escribió Harfuch. El martes, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo ante Naciones Unidas que México era el epicentro de la violencia de los cárteles de la droga, y añadió que el país debía recuperar el control de su territorio.

item.content:encoded: Bei anhaltend hohen Energiepreisen ist laut Bundesbankchef Joachim Nagel ein konjunkturdämpfender Kurs der EZB nicht auszuschließen. Er erklärte, das Zinsniveau von derzeit 2,5 Prozent bewege sich in einem Bereich, der die Konjunktur weder dämpfe noch anschiebe: "Ich kann nicht ausschließen, dass wir bei anhaltend hohen Energiepreisen in einen Bereich leicht restriktiver Geldpolitik übergehen müssen", fügte er am Dienstagabend in London hinzu. Er relativierte jedoch Befürchtungen hinsichtlich Zweitrundeneffekten bei der Inflation. Damit sind Auswirkungen der vom Iran-Krieg hochgetriebenen Energiekosten gemeint, die zu einer Lohn-Preis-Spirale führen können und die starke Teuerung damit verfestigen. Nagel verwies darauf, dass sich der Arbeitsmarkt deutlich weniger angespannt präsentiere als im Jahr 2022. Damals hatte die durch Energiepreise getriebene Inflation zu steigenden Lohnforderungen und einer Lohn-Preis-Spirale geführt. Der Bundesbankchef sagte, die Ölpreise spielten für die Währungshüter bei der Festlegung der Leitzinsen eine zunehmend wichtigere Rolle, aber auch andere Faktoren seien im Fokus. Ähnlich hatte sich zuvor bereits EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde geäußert und damit Spekulationen über eine mögliche Zinserhöhung im Oktober die Spitze genommen. An den Finanzmärkten wird es für wahrscheinlich gehalten, dass die EZB im Dezember mit einer weiteren Zinserhöhung nachlegen wird - es wäre die dritte in diesem Jahr.

item.title: Swiss upper house backs 90% CET1 capital backing for UBS foreign units
item.description: In a blow to UBS, Switzerland's upper house of parliament on Wednesday voted in favour of capital rules that would require the bank to back its foreign units with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: In a blow to UBS (UBSG.S) , Switzerland's upper house of parliament on Wednesday voted in favour of capital rules that would require the bank to back its foreign units with 90% Common Equity Tier 1 capital. Following the decision in the first of two chambers, the capital rules bill will move to the lower house of parliament, with a final decision expected at the end of this year at the earliest, and more likely in 2027.

item.title: 'Super' El Niño could cause 451,000 excess deaths, researchers say
item.description: Extreme heat caused by this year's "super-El Niño" could result in as many as 451,000 excess deaths across the globe in the six months through February 2027, researchers with the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Extreme heat caused by this year's "super-El Niño" could result in as many as 451,000 excess deaths across the globe in the six months through February 2027, researchers with the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab said on Wednesday. The number of extremely hot days is likely to rise by 44% compared to normal years, Climate Impact Lab said in a report . The country likely to suffer the most excess heat-related fatalities from September 2026 to February 2027 is Nigeria with 31,400, followed by Indonesia with 19,300 and Sudan with 17,600. Heat in Africa's Sahel region, including Niger and Chad as well as Nigeria and Sudan, is likely to cause an additional 66,800 deaths over the six-month period. The researchers project the Philippines, Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia to see an additional 19,400 deaths combined. The number of excess deaths could even climb higher if El Niño extends further into 2027, with key areas of the northern hemisphere, including India and Pakistan, especially vulnerable during their summer months. Climate Impact Lab described this year's El Niño as a "postcard from the future", delivering temperatures that will become normal in just a few decades. It said emergency response efforts should be directed to high-priority regions to tackle heat-related mortality in the coming months. "This report allows decision makers to see exactly where emergency actions can be taken now to save tens of thousands of lives in the coming months," said Michael Greenstone, economist at the University of Chicago and co-founder of the lab.

item.title: El IBEX estira el repunte con Irán y la cumbre Trump-Xi en el foco
item.description: El IBEX 35 abrió el miércoles con un alza moderada y prolongaba la subida de las dos sesiones previas, aunque el repunte mostraba síntomas de agotamiento a la espera de nuevos alicientes para el riesgo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El IBEX 35 abrió el miércoles con un alza moderada y prolongaba la subida de las dos sesiones previas, aunque el repunte mostraba síntomas de agotamiento a la espera de nuevos alicientes para el riesgo. El mejor tono se apoyaba en el respiro del petróleo, con el Brent por debajo de los 100 dólares por barril, en parte por la sorprendente rapidez con la que Arabia Saudí [USN:L6N45E0PV TEXT:"está restableciendo"] los flujos a través de su oleoducto Este-Oeste. En el plano geopolítico, Teherán aseguró haber contactado con Estados Unidos a través de un mediador catarí en Nueva York para presentar sus condiciones de cara a la apertura del estrecho de Ormuz, si bien la mayoría de ellas ya habían sido rechazadas con anterioridad. El presidente Trump afirmó ante Naciones Unidas que las conversaciones habían avanzado, pese a que lleva meses repitiendo mensajes similares, y generó nuevas dudas al [USN:L6N45E0R4 TEXT:"amenazar con aniquilar a Irán"]. El presidente iraní, Masud Pezeshkian, se dirige hoy a la Asamblea General de la ONU y el mercado está pendiente de las informaciones que apuntan a un posible encuentro con Trump. Las esperanzas de un acuerdo entre EEUU e Irán que permita a este país reconstruirse y convertirse en una potencia económica en la región infundían un optimismo cauteloso en los mercados financieros, según la casa de valores Renta 4. "Esta expectativa alivia temporalmente las expectativas de inflación y, por derivada, de tipos de intervención, aunque seguimos sin tener un acuerdo claro y definitivo que resuelva la incertidumbre geopolítica", señalaron estos analistas en su informe previo a la apertura de las bolsas europeas. En paralelo, el presidente chino, Xi Jinping, llega a Washington a lo largo del día en medio de la especulación sobre una posible prórroga de la tregua comercial entre Washington y Pekín y una eventual cooperación en materia de inteligencia artificial. El apetito de los consumidores por las aplicaciones de IA seguía impulsando a los valores tecnológicos, con el tirón del asistente Muse, de Meta, aún vigente como prueba de que los usuarios pueden animarse a adoptar agentes de inteligencia artificial de forma masiva. Los analistas se muestran ahora expectantes ante la acogida que tendrá un producto similar de Google Labs, conocido como CC. Con todo, persistía la preocupación por el endurecimiento de las condiciones de financiación en todo el mundo ante el repunte de la inflación derivado de la guerra en Oriente Medio. El presidente de la Fed de Richmond, [USN:L6N45E0Y2 TEXT:"Tom Barkin"], y la presidenta de la Fed de Boston, [USN:L6N45E0OC TEXT:"Susan Collins"], respaldaron el martes la subida de tipos de la semana pasada, dada la inquietud por el alza de los precios. Los mercados de futuros descuentan una probabilidad del 54% de que la Fed vuelva a subir los tipos en octubre y anticipan 33 puntos básicos de endurecimiento para final de año . La atención de la jornada se centrará, además, en los PMI preliminares de septiembre en Europa, Reino Unido y Estados Unidos, así como en las intervenciones del gobernador de la Fed Michael Barr y de varios dirigentes del BCE, entre ellos Pedro Machado, Piero Cipollone, Philip Lane, y Boris Vujcic. A las 0700 GMT del miércoles, el selectivo bursátil español IBEX 35 (.IBEX) subía 117,30 puntos, un 0,59%, hasta 19.871,40 puntos, mientras que el índice de grandes valores europeos FTSE Eurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) avanzaba un 0,38%. En el sector bancario, Santander (SAN.MC) subía un 0,65%, BBVA (BBVA.MC) se anotaba un 0,88%, Caixabank (CABK.MC) avanzaba un 1,81%, Sabadell (SABE.MC) ganaba un 1,06%, Bankinter (BKT.MC) se revalorizaba un 1,11% y Unicaja Banco (UNI.MC) subía un 1,07%. Entre los grandes valores no financieros, Telefónica (TEF.MC) se anotaba un 0,40%, Inditex (ITX.MC) avanzaba un 0,34%, Iberdrola (IBE.MC) apenas mostraba variaciones, Cellnex (CLNX.MC) ganaba un 0,12% y la petrolera Repsol (REP.MC) subía un 0,54%.

item.title: Argentina's Milei addresses UN as tensions rise over Falkland Islands
item.description: Argentina's President Javier Milei on Wednesday will address world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly amid escalating tensions with Britain over oil exploration around the Falkland Islands, a largely self-governing British overseas territory whose sovereignty Argentina has long disputed.
item.dc:creator: Leila Miller
item.content:encoded: Argentina's President Javier Milei on Wednesday will address world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly amid escalating tensions with Britain over oil exploration around the Falkland Islands, a largely self-governing British overseas territory whose sovereignty Argentina has long disputed. Argentina earlier this month began sanctions proceedings against more than [USN:S0N43N05D TEXT:" 60 companies and people"] linked to an offshore oil drilling project, a move that British officials have strongly pushed back on. British Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Overseas Territories Uma Kumaran in a statement on Friday called Argentina's actions "unacceptable," saying that "the Falkland Islands are British and they have the right to develop their natural resources as they see fit." Milei is likely to reaffirm Argentina's actions in his UN speech, analysts and political commentators say. On Thursday, he is due to meet with Israeli Prime Minister and close ally Benjamin Netanyahu. The Falklands oil drilling project has [USN:L6N44W0IS TEXT:"strong Israeli ties."] Argentina’s sovereignty claim to the islands in the South Atlantic that it calls the Malvinas remains central [USN:L6N44W125 TEXT:"to its national identity"]. The country invaded the archipelago in 1982 and fought a 10-week war that ended with Argentina's surrender to Britain and is still commemorated in Buenos Aires in street murals for the fallen soldiers. In a televised address this month, Milei said the drilling project violates a 1976 UN General Assembly resolution urging both countries to resolve the sovereignty dispute through dialogue and avoid unilateral decisions. His speech came days after US President Donald Trump, a Milei ally, suggested Washington could reconsider its traditionally neutral position on the Falklands dispute. 'SHIFT THE AGENDA' Milei's tougher stance marks a notable shift for a president who had been criticized by political opponents for showing little interest in the sovereignty dispute while pursuing closer ties with the US and Europe. Now Argentina’s opposition is accusing Milei, who is expected to seek reelection in 2027, of using the dispute to bolster domestic support. "It's simply something to look good in the eyes of society or to try to shift the agenda," said Guillermo Michel, a Peronist opposition congressman in the chamber of deputies. However, a study by the Buenos Aires-based consultancy Inteligencia Analitica found that his televised address produced only a modest improvement in his public image. “The Malvinas issue in Argentina transcends the president’s speech,” said Marcelo Escolar, the firm's director. Last week, [USN:L1N4590CV TEXT:"Milei presented"] a bill that aims to toughen sanctions on those deemed to unlawfully participate in activities utilizing natural resources in Argentina's maritime spaces and continental shelf. The bill will first be referred to committee, as the government weighs its legislative priorities. Milei lacks a majority in Congress but has managed to pass important economic reforms. Marcelo Seghini, a defense adviser in the lower house, said that while some parts of the sovereignty bill may have bipartisan support, other provisions unrelated to the Falklands dispute may spur opposition. Owners of the [USN:L6N44W0IS TEXT:"Sea Lion offshore project"], Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration, have indicated they do not expect Milei's actions to derail development.

item.title: The global energy transition shifts from generation to integration
item.description: Global electric grids are entering a new phase, with investment spending by utilities shifting from solar panels and wind farms toward the infrastructure needed to make renewable-heavy power systems work.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Maguire
item.content:encoded: Global electric grids are entering a new phase, with investment spending by utilities shifting from solar panels and wind farms toward the infrastructure needed to make renewable-heavy power systems work. Across Europe, Asia, Africa, Oceania and Latin America, demand for batteries and grid equipment is still climbing even as purchases of solar systems retreat from earlier peaks, signalling a shift in focus from building renewable capacity to strengthening the infrastructure needed to support it. The shift reflects the rising complexity of operating power systems with large volumes of renewable energy. Many markets now have enough solar capacity to produce substantial electricity surpluses during sunny periods, placing greater value on batteries, transmission assets and grid upgrades that can store, balance and redistribute that power. As a result, investment is increasingly flowing toward the infrastructure that determines how effectively renewable electricity can be used rather than how much can be generated. SOLAR IN RETREAT? Data on global imports of China-made solar systems show a remarkable slowdown in purchases of what have become one of the defining features of global energy transition efforts: solar panels. After peaking at over $5.8 billion in March of 2023, global imports of China-made photovoltaic solar systems have recently dropped to less than half of that amount, and so far in 2026 have averaged $2.7 billion a month, data from Ember shows. However, rather than evidence of permanently declining interest, the slower uptake of solar arrays may be a sign that China's solar panels have been a victim of their own success. Forty different countries — from Australia to Pakistan to Nigeria — have spent over $1 billion on imports of Chinese solar systems since the start of 2018, including 12 nations that have spent in excess of $5 billion. That kind of money buys a lot of panels, and has resulted in a surge in solar generation capacity. The utilities running those power systems now need tools to manage the fluxes in clean power production that come with hefty solar footprints. TOOLS OF THE (UTILITY) TRADE To make maximum use of the growing volumes of solar power flowing through their grids, utilities across the world are turning to battery storage systems and real-time grid management components in record numbers. And as with the renewable energy generation assets, China is the world's top grid equipment and battery manufacturer and exporter. This has resulted in the value of China's exports of batteries and grid equipment surging to record highs in 2026, even as total sales of solar systems hold at roughly half their peak. During the first seven months of 2026, global importers paid roughly $75 billion for Chinese energy storage batteries and grid equipment, Ember data shows. That total is roughly $20 billion larger than during the same months in 2025, and compares to around $19.4 billion for solar imports so far in 2026. Europe was the top region for battery and grid import purchases, with the region coughing up around $31.1 billion on those components, followed by Asia's $22 billion. Latin America and Africa also dialled up battery and grid imports to record highs so far this year to around $3.9 billion and $3.8 billion respectively, while imports by Oceania also hit an all-time high of just over $3.6 billion. Imports by the Middle East declined slightly to around $3.1 billion, due mainly to heavy disruptions to regional economic activity and logistics flows stemming from the war against Iran. Battery and grid imports into North America also posted a year-over-year decline to around $7 billion, due in large part to hefty tariffs on China-made products. FULLY UTILIZED All told, these purchases of battery systems and grid components allow utilities to store excess solar output during sunny periods, and release that electricity during peak consumption spells. For utilities, that ability to store surplus power for later use helps reduce system-wide curtailment of renewable energy assets, smoothes power price volatility and reduces curtailment of renewable assets within power networks. Greater battery capacity and enhanced grid capabilities also aid in capping generation from fossil fuel power plants, which require expensive and constant fuel renewal — often via complex international trade routes that can be impacted by geopolitical upheaval. Those benefits look set to keep China-made batteries and grid equipment in high demand for the near term at least, and should ensure that China's broader clean technology sector continues to enjoy brisk export earnings even as solar sales hit saturation point in several markets. In that sense, the slowdown in solar imports is less a sign of fading momentum than of a maturing transition. Many power systems now have substantial renewable generation capacity in place, and the investment focus is shifting toward the assets needed to fully utilise that capacity. The countries that make the most progress over the coming decade may therefore be distinguished less by how many solar panels they install than by how rapidly they can build the tools needed to put every available kilowatt-hour of electricity to work. item.title: Portugal says entry into grid operator REN won't affect China's State Grid
item.description: Portugal's government said its acquisition of a stake in power and gas grid operator REN would have no implications for the 25% stake held by China's State Grid, which it wants to remain a key shareholder.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Goncalves
item.content:encoded: Portugal's government said its acquisition of a stake in power and gas grid operator REN (RENE.LS) would have no implications for the 25% stake held by China's State Grid, which it wants to remain a key shareholder. The state agreed last month to [USN:L6N44C02Q TEXT:"buy 13.7% of REN"], returning to the company 12 years after exiting during Portugal's bailout, a period that saw the Chinese state-owned utility acquire a 25% stake and become its largest shareholder. The Portuguese government plans to increase its holding to as much as 20%. The Finance Ministry said in a statement late on Tuesday that Lisbon had informed Beijing that the state's entry into REN's capital would not imply any change to State Grid's 25% stake. "On the contrary, it is in the Portuguese government's interest for State Grid to remain a reference shareholder in REN," it said. The ministry said growing geopolitical uncertainty and the increasing strategic importance of energy infrastructure justified its investment in REN, arguing that electricity and gas networks are critical to energy security, the energy transition, industrial development and attracting investment. It said the move "forms part of a global trend towards greater government involvement in strategic sectors", noting that Portugal had been the only European Union member state without a state stake in its national electricity grid operator. The ministry said most EU countries retain state ownership or significant state shareholdings in their national electricity grid operators. It said the investment would give the state greater oversight of a strategic asset and help align REN's long-term strategy with national priorities. "Geopolitical changes and the growing importance of energy, and electricity in particular, especially in the push to electrify the economy and attract investment in artificial intelligence and data centres, also justify the decision," it said.

item.title: South Africa faces $8 billion bill to revive state-owned refineries
item.description: South Africa will need more than $8 billion to revive two mothballed state-owned refineries, officials told lawmakers, as the country seeks to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imported fuels.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa will need more than $8 billion to revive two mothballed state-owned refineries, officials told lawmakers, as the country seeks to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imported fuels. South Africa's state-owned Central Energy Fund acquired the flood-damaged 180,000 barrels-per-day Sapref refinery in 2024 from BP (BP.L) and Shell (SHEL.L) for a token 1 rand ($0.0617). CEF said it plans to revive the refinery's liquefied petroleum gas import and distribution business and lease out existing storage tanks to generate early revenue. The plan is to upgrade the refinery to a 400,000 to 650,000 bpd plant with National Treasury approval and a final investment decision targeted for 2027/28, the CEF said in a statement late on Monday. The total refinery investment is expected to cost around $7.15 billion, CEF said, without providing funding details. One banking source and one government source said they were discussing potential financing from the pan-African Afreximbank, among others. The CEF is weighing plans to revive its Mossel Bay gas-to-liquids refinery, which has been idle since 2020 due to a shortage of domestic gas feedstock. The Mossel Bay GTL refinery, operated by PetroSA and now part of the South African National Petroleum Company, will be restarted in phases. Phase 1 targets around 18,000 bpd at an estimated investment of 5.8 billion rand. Phase 2, targeting production of 46,000 bpd, will require an extra R8.5 billion ($525.35 million). ($1 = 16.1797 rand)

item.title: Dodgers extend home winning streak to 11 with shutout of Padres
item.description: Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and the Los Angeles Dodgers inched closer to the best record in the National League with a 7-0 victory over the visiting San Diego Padres in the opener of a three-game series Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and the Los Angeles Dodgers inched closer to the best record in the National League with a 7-0 victory over the visiting San Diego Padres in the opener of a three-game series Tuesday. Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games. Los Angeles moved to within one game of the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the NL Division Series to one. Rookie designated hitter Josue De Paula had two hits with a run scored for the Dodgers, with Shohei Ohtani expected to return from a biceps injury as a hitter Wednesday. Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two. Right-hander Michael King (12-10) gave up five runs on six hits over four innings, his most runs allowed in a start since May 30. It was just the second loss in 15 games for San Diego, which is close to locking up a third consecutive playoff berth for the first time in franchise history. The Dodgers took advantage of King's loss of command to start a four-run outburst in the second inning, all with two outs. The Dodgers loaded the bases on two singles and a hit batter, while Edman and Mookie Betts both walked to force in runs. Freeman followed Betts with a two-run single for a 4-0 lead. Freeman added a run-scoring single in the fourth inning, while Edman hit a home run in the sixth and Smith hit his in the seventh. Edman homered for the second straight game, while Smith went deep in his third consecutive start. item.title: MLB roundup: Drew Rasmussen helps Rays smother Yankees for AL East title
item.description: Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader. The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy Diaz drove in four runs on a pair of singles. Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left for New York. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly. Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start. Yankees 2, Rays 0 (Game 1) Cody Bellinger hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning as host New York recorded a shutout over Tampa Bay in the opener of a day-night doubleheader. With the victory, the Yankees temporarily prevented the Rays from clinching the AL East and moved six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot. New York's Carlos Rodon (7-3) scattered three singles over eight innings as the Yankees finished off the victory in a brisk 2 hours, 2 minutes. Rodon struck out eight in his 100th career win and also reached 1,500 strikeouts for his career. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5) allowed two runs on five hits over six innings with seven strikeouts to take his first loss since July 9. Dodgers 7, Padres 0 Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and Los Angeles inched closer to the best record in the National League with a shutout of visiting San Diego. Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games. Los Angeles moved to within one game of the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the National League Division Series to one. Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two. Phillies 6, Brewers 4 Bryson Stott delivered the tiebreaking hit in the eighth inning to guide Philadelphia to a victory over visiting Milwaukee. Brandon Marsh homered and knocked in three runs as the Phillies lowered their magic number to two to clinch a postseason berth. Zack Wheeler ended up with a no-decision after striking out 11 while giving up three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Wheeler struck out the first seven batters he faced, setting a Phillies record for consecutive strikeouts to begin a game. His first-inning strikeout of Brice Turang was the 2,000th of his career. The Brewers saw their lead over the Dodgers for the top record in the majors shrink to one as they lost just the third time in their last 13 games. William Contreras knocked in three runs. Marlins 8, Cubs 2 (12 innings) Griffin Conine plated the go-ahead run that ignited a six-run 12th inning for visiting Miami, which snapped a three-game losing by beating Chicago and postponing the Cubs' playoff celebration for at least a day. On a night when runs were scarce until the final inning, both teams endured a pair of scoreless extra frames before Conine broke the drought with a leadoff, golf-shot single off Caleb Thielbar that fell just inside the left field line. Esteury Ruiz, the automatic runner, scored from second to make it 3-2 as the Marlins sent 10 batters to the plate in the inning. The Cubs could have clinched a wild-card playoff spot with a win or Arizona loss, but neither of those happened keeping the Diamondbacks mathematically alive. Josh Ekness (3-4) struck out a pair in the 11th inning to get the win while Thielbar (3-4) gave up three runs -- two earned -- in his inning of work. Guardians 3, Red Sox 2 Nathaniel Lowe drove in Chase DeLauter with a sacrifice fly in the ninth inning and Cleveland held on to beat host Boston in the first game of a three-game series. Cleveland not only extended its winning streak to six but maintained its one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for first place in the AL Central. Parker Messick held Boston to one run on five hits in five innings, his 14th straight start allowing three runs or fewer. Payton Tolle started for the Red Sox and gave up two runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Guardians went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 15. White Sox 14, Royals 11 Chase Meidroth smacked a three-run home run among his three hits and drove in five, and Brenton Doyle, Randal Grichuk and Munetaka Murakami also homered to power Chicago past host Kansas City. Chicago won for the fourth time in five games to remain one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox, who hold the third and final AL wild-card spot, reduced their magic number to earn a playoff berth to three. Vinnie Pasquantino hit a ninth-inning grand slam for the Royals, who lost their fifth straight. He went 3-for-5 with a double and also drove in five. Nationals 3, Tigers 1 CJ Abrams hit a pair of home runs and drove in all three runs as visiting Washington topped Detroit. Abrams reached 100 RBIs for the season with his solo shot in the second inning, then broke a 1-1 tie in the seventh with his 33rd long ball of the season, a two-run blast. Dylan Crews had two hits and scored the other run for the Nationals. Rookie Jackson Kent (2-4) earned the win in long relief. He allowed one run on six hits over four innings and struck out three. Opener Riley Cornelio lasted 2 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking three. Ben Malgeri scored the Tigers' only run. Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark each had two hits. Pirates 2, Cardinals 0 Jared Jones and two relievers combined on a one-hitter as Pittsburgh beat visiting St. Louis for a fifth straight win. Jones (5-6) lowered his ERA to 1.08 in four September starts and struck out nine with zero walks over seven innings while throwing 63 of his 86 pitches for strikes. Pittsburgh broke a scoreless tie with two outs in the sixth inning on Ryan O'Hearn's RBI single against Andre Pallante (12-8). Pallante allowed one run on three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over six innings. St. Louis struck out 14 times and lost for the fifth time in its last six games. Astros 7, Mariners 0 Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as Houston slugged and pitched its way past host Seattle. Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros, who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the West. Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings of relief. Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle. The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine. Cincinnati ended a two-game losing streak and evened the season series with Atlanta at 2-2. Williamson (5-4) worked six scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two strikeouts. Elly De La Cruz (29), Dane Myers (8) and Eugenio Suarez (25) each hit a home run for the Reds. It was Suarez's 350th career homer, making him the 10th active player to reach that mark. Atlanta starter JR Ritchie (1-4) pitched five innings and allowed one run on four hits and three walks. The rookie struck out a career-high eight batters. Mets 6, Rangers 3 Francisco Alvarez laced a go-ahead two-run double in the sixth, then scored an insurance run on an unusual sacrifice fly for visiting New York, who damaged Texas' playoff hopes with a win in the opener of a three-game interleague series in Arlington. Juan Soto had an RBI single in the third, and Carson Benge capped the scoring with a run-scoring double in the seventh for the Mets. The club won hours after removing the interim tag from manager Andy Green and signing him to a three-year extension. Josh Jung had an RBI double in the third, and Elias Diaz and Wyatt Langford lofted sacrifice flies in the fourth for the Rangers, who entered Tuesday with a one-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West. Diamondbacks 7, Rockies 2 Nolan Arenado homered and doubled among his three hits, Michael Soroka tossed seven strong innings, and Arizona kept its slim postseason hopes alive with a win over host Colorado in Denver. Geraldo Perdomo also had three hits and Ildemaro Vargas finished with two hits for Arizona, which remains alive in the NL wild-card race, sitting four games behind Philadelphia, San Diego and the Chicago Cubs for the third and final spot with five games to go. Mickey Moniak homered for Colorado, which finished with just three hits and just one after the third inning. The Rockies (57-100) are the first team to lose 100 or more games in four straight seasons since the 1962-65 New York Mets. Twins 3, Giants 2 Walker Jenkins homered, Luke Keaschall contributed both offensively and defensively, and Minnesota evened its road interleague series against San Francisco. Taj Bradley (12-6) combined with four relievers on a six-hitter for the Twins, who used two late diving catches by Keaschall in right field to prevent the Giants from taking the first two of the series. Bradley allowed just one other hit -- a fifth-inning single by Drew Gilbert -- in his six innings. He walked three and struck out six. Keaschall's one-out triple scored Ryan Kreidler, then Brooks Lee gave Minnesota the lead for good with a run-scoring single to plate Keaschall. A's 9, Angels 7 Carlos Cortes hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the bottom of the eighth inning and the Athletics overcame a six-run deficit to beat Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif. In addition to the homer off Sam Bachman, Cortes also delivered a pinch-hit RBI triple in the seventh, helping the Athletics end a six-game losing streak. Zack Gelof hit a two-run homer later in the eighth for the A's. Shea Langeliers and Lawrence Butler each had three hits and an RBI for the Athletics. Denzer Guzman homered and drove in four RBIs for the Angels, who have lost four of their last six games. Mike Trout added three hits and two runs for Los Angeles (60-97), which has never lost 100 games in a season. Blue Jays at Orioles, ppd. item.title: Marruecos vota para elegir el Gobierno encargado del plan para el Mundial de fútbol
item.description: Los marroquíes acuden este miércoles a las urnas en unas elecciones que determinarán la composición del Gobierno encargado de gestionar las fases finales de un plan de 20.000 millones de dólares destinado a preparar el Mundial de 2030, así como de proyectos para canalizar los beneficios económicos hacia la desilusionada juventud del país.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
item.content:encoded: Los marroquíes acuden este miércoles a las urnas en unas elecciones que determinarán la composición del Gobierno encargado de gestionar las fases finales de un plan de 20.000 millones de dólares destinado a preparar el Mundial de 2030, así como de proyectos para canalizar los beneficios económicos hacia la desilusionada juventud del país. No se espera que las elecciones parlamentarias alteren de forma significativa el equilibrio de poder en Marruecos, donde el rey conserva amplios poderes sobre la orientación política, la defensa y los asuntos exteriores. Sin embargo, el próximo parlamento tendrá la tarea de poner en marcha iniciativas cada vez más orientadas a abordar el descontento juvenil, que quedó patente con la avalancha masiva en la frontera con el enclave español de Ceuta y en las protestas mortales lideradas por la Generación Z el año pasado. El actual Gobierno está formado por tres partidos —entre ellos dos fundados por personas cercanas a la casa real— que desbancaron a un partido islamista moderado que había llegado al poder una década antes, tras las protestas de la Primavera Árabe de 2011. Esas manifestaciones llevaron al rey a ceder más competencias a un parlamento elegido, antes de reafirmar posteriormente su control sobre ámbitos como los asuntos exteriores y el Ministerio del Interior. En virtud de la Constitución aprobada en 2011, el rey nombra al primer ministro del partido que obtenga la mayor proporción de los 395 escaños del Parlamento. A continuación, el primer ministro debe negociar una coalición antes de presentar una lista de miembros del Gobierno para su aprobación real. Los colegios electorales abrirán a las 8.00 horas (0800 GMT) y cerrarán a las 19.00 horas (1900 GMT), y los resultados preliminares suelen anunciarse al día siguiente de las elecciones. La participación, especialmente entre los votantes jóvenes, será objeto de especial atención, ya que se considerará un barómetro de la confianza de los ciudadanos en las instituciones. Aproximadamente 27 millones de marroquíes tienen edad para votar, pero solo 15,8 millones están inscritos en el censo electoral, lo que supone un descenso de alrededor del 12% con respecto a las elecciones de 2021. PLANES DE GASTO Los dos principales partidos del actual Parlamento, el partido gobernante Agrupación Nacional de Independientes (RNI) y el Partido de la Autenticidad y la Modernidad (PAM), se han comprometido a crear alrededor de un millón de puestos de trabajo durante la próxima legislatura de cinco años, y han prometido mejorar la vivienda, los salarios y los hospitales. Ambos gobiernan juntos en una coalición, pero durante la campaña se han culpado mutuamente por no haber frenado la subida de los precios de los alimentos y por otras deficiencias políticas. Debido a estos desacuerdos, los líderes del PAM han descartado formar otra coalición con el RNI en caso de resultar ganadores. El primer ministro Aziz Akhannouch, un empresario multimillonario que ha liderado el Gobierno desde 2021, no se presenta de nuevo tras haber dimitido este año como líder del RNI. Fouzi Lekjaa, ministro de Presupuesto, presidente de la Federación Marroquí de Fútbol y presidente del comité organizador de la fase final del Mundial de fútbol de 2030, se incorporó a la dirección del PAM unas semanas antes de las elecciones. Marruecos está realizando importantes inversiones en estadios, ferrocarriles y otras infraestructuras de cara al Mundial, que coorganizará con España y Portugal, y tiene como objetivo duplicar la producción económica per cápita para 2035. El Fondo Monetario Internacional ha estimado el gasto previsto en unos 190.000 millones de dirhams, es decir, unos 20.000 millones de dólares, lo que supone casi el 12% de su producto interior bruto en 2024. Entre los demás partidos que se disputan el poder se encuentran el Partido Istiqlal (PI), nacionalista y de tendencia conservadora, actualmente en el poder; el Partido de la Justicia y el Desarrollo (PJD), islamista, que sufrió una derrota aplastante en las últimas elecciones; y varios partidos de izquierda.

item.title: Musk elogia a Xi como un gran líder en una entrevista con la televisión estatal china
item.description: El director ejecutivo de Tesla Inc, Elon Musk, elogió al presidente chino Xi Jinping calificándolo de "gran líder" en unas declaraciones durante una entrevista con la cadena de televisión estatal china CCTV el miércoles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El director ejecutivo de Tesla Inc, Elon Musk, elogió al presidente chino Xi Jinping calificándolo de "gran líder" en unas declaraciones durante una entrevista con la cadena de televisión estatal china CCTV el miércoles. "Bajo su mandato, China ha prosperado enormemente", afirmó Musk, señalando los avances que se observan en los nuevos edificios y las infraestructuras construidas en el país. "También resulta evidente, con solo pasear por las calles, la mayor prosperidad del ciudadano chino medio", añadió. Está previsto que Musk se una a otros directores ejecutivos estadounidenses en una cena de Estado en la Casa Blanca ofrecida por el presidente Donald Trump en honor a Xi el jueves, informó Reuters. Xi se reunirá con Trump este jueves en la segunda cumbre de este año entre los líderes de las dos mayores economías del mundo. Musk también se refirió al mayor centro de fabricación de Tesla, situado en Shanghái, y calificó al equipo de "increíblemente talentoso, trabajador y de confianza". "La fábrica de Tesla en Shanghái es una joya y, de hecho, es preciosa, si es que alguien ha estado allí alguna vez", afirmó. Musk ya había desmentido anteriormente las especulaciones de que las operaciones de Tesla en China pudieran separarse de cara a una posible fusión con SpaceX. Las ventas de los vehículos Model 3 y Model Y fabricados en la planta de Tesla en Shanghái —que es también su mayor centro de exportación a nivel mundial— aumentaron un 3,6% interanual en agosto, lo que supone una marcada desaceleración con respecto al mes anterior, ya que persistieron las tendencias divergentes en los principales mercados del fabricante de automóviles estadounidense.

item.title: How does New Zealand's electoral system work and does it favour coalitions?
item.description: New Zealand 54th parliament sits for its final time this week ahead of a Nov. 7 election. Polls indicate that no one party will emerge as a clear winner with neck-to-neck support for both left and right blocks.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Craymer
item.content:encoded: New Zealand 54th parliament sits for its final time this week ahead of a Nov. 7 election. Polls indicate that no one party will emerge as a clear winner with neck-to-neck support for both left and right blocks. The winning group would be decided based on a mixed-member proportional (MMP) electoral system, which has made coalitions the norm in New Zealand since it was introduced three-decades ago. WHAT IS MMP? New Zealand switched from a British first-past-the-post system, in which the top finisher in each electoral district wins the seat, to MMP on the recommendation of a commission addressing concerns that smaller parties were being left out. All governments under MMP have been coalitions of the centre-left Labour or centre-right National with the support of smaller parties, except in 2020 when the Labour government swept to power after successfully managing the early months of the COVID-19 outbreak. Originating in Germany, MMP has been adopted, sometimes with modifications, in countries including Bolivia, Lesotho, South Korea and Thailand. HOW IT WORKS Under MMP, voters cast two votes: one for their preferred constituency candidate and one for a party. The candidate with the most votes wins and becomes an MP, while the party vote decides how many seats each party gets in parliament. The winning candidates of the country's 71 constituencies take their seats automatically, while the remaining seats are filled from party lists, allocated to match each party’s share of the nationwide vote. There are expected to be about 49 party list seats in this election, though that number can change. Political parties must get at least 5% of the party vote or win at least one electorate seat to get any seats in Parliament. A party or coalition can form a government when it secures a majority in the single-chamber parliament, usually at least 61 of 120 seats. KINGMAKERS Due to the nature of the MMP electoral system that was first used in New Zealand in 1996, minor parties often play a decisive role in forming the government. New Zealand First has been the most prominent kingmaker, backing National after the 1996 election and Labour after the 2017 election. Te Pati Maori has also helped larger parties govern, supporting National-led governments after the 2008, 2011 and 2014 elections. In this election, the centrist Opportunity Party could also become pivotal if it reaches the 5% party-vote threshold or wins an electorate seat. The 2017 election showed how the largest party does not always end up in power. National won 56 seats, more than Labour's 46, but was unable to assemble a majority. Labour formed a government through a coalition with New Zealand First and a confidence-and-supply agreement with the Green Party. QUIRKS Parliament normally has 120 seats, but extra seats can be added when a party wins more electorate seats than its share of the nationwide party vote would otherwise entitle it to. This happened after the 2023 election, when Te Pati Māora won six electorates while receiving 3.1% of the party vote. Polls indicate this could happen again in 2026. In the system, seven of the electorate seats are Maori electorates, reserved for voters who choose to enrol on the Maori electoral roll. Maori voters can choose to enrol in a general electorate.

item.title: New Zealand parliament adjourns before November election
item.description: New Zealand's parliament wrapped up its final sitting on Wednesday before a Nov. 7 election, with party leaders using the closing debate to press their competing cases to voters ahead of what is expected to be a close poll.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Craymer
item.content:encoded: New Zealand's parliament wrapped up its final sitting on Wednesday before a Nov. 7 election, with party leaders using the closing debate to press their competing cases to voters ahead of what is expected to be a close poll. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon hailed his centre-right government's record, while opposition Labour leader Chris Hipkins accused it of failing to deliver on its central promises during the three-year term. "I'm incredibly proud of what this government has achieved," Luxon said in his final speech to parliament, listing economic growth, record exports and lower government debt among the coalition's achievements. "We know in the National Party this is the greatest country on earth with extraordinary potential still to realise if we make the right choice (at the election)," he said, turning his remarks into a pitch for a second term. Opinion polls suggest a closely contested election, with neither the centre-right governing bloc nor parties on the left consistently showing a clear path to a parliamentary majority. The campaign is expected to focus on the cost of living, economic management and public services, as Luxon's National Party seeks to retain office possibly alongside its coalition partners ACT New Zealand and New Zealand First. Opposition leader Hipkins said the government had failed to ease pressure on households. "They promised to fix the cost of living. They have made everything worse for New Zealanders. This is a government that's had the wrong priorities. That's been out of touch with New Zealanders," Hipkins told parliament. "This government has completely failed to do the thing that it promised to do. This government are out of ideas and they are now out of time." Parliament is due to be formally dissolved on October 1, beginning the formal election period ahead of the vote.

item.title: El precio del petróleo es cada vez más importante para el BCE, según el presidente del Bundesbank
item.description: Los precios del crudo son un indicador cada vez más importante para los responsables del BCE a la hora de fijar las tasas de interés, pero hay otros factores que también desempeñan un papel crucial, dijo el martes el presidente del Bundesbank, Joachim Nagel, después de que los mercados aumentaran las expectativas de subida de tasas debido al elevado costo de la energía.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Los precios del crudo son un indicador cada vez más importante para los responsables del BCE a la hora de fijar las tasas de interés, pero hay otros factores que también desempeñan un papel crucial, dijo el martes el presidente del Bundesbank, Joachim Nagel, después de que los mercados aumentaran las expectativas de subida de tasas debido al elevado costo de la energía. El BCE ya ha subido su tasa de interés de referencia en dos ocasiones este verano boreal, pero los inversionistas prevén otras tres o cuatro subidas durante el próximo año, ya que tanto los precios del petróleo como los del gas se sitúan ahora en su escenario "grave" y la inflación podría alcanzar un máximo en torno al 4%, el doble del objetivo del banco. Tanto la presidenta del BCE, Christine Lagarde, como el vicepresidente, Boris Vujcic, han rebatido esas previsiones, argumentando que las tasas de interés no varían al compás de los precios del petróleo. Sus declaraciones indicaban que el banco podría esperar hasta diciembre para dar el siguiente paso. "Sin duda no es el único indicador, pero se ha convertido en un indicador más relevante en los últimos cuatro años, eso es seguro", afirmó Nagel en un acto organizado por la Sociedad de Economistas Profesionales de Londres. "Es obvio que nosotros, en el Consejo de Gobierno, tenemos que tenerlo en cuenta y debemos considerarlo a la hora de tomar nuestras decisiones", dijo en referencia a los precios del petróleo. No obstante, dejó la puerta abierta a nuevas subidas de tasas. Dijo que las tasas, que actualmente se sitúan en el 2,5%, se encuentran en un nivel que ni restringe ni estimula el crecimiento económico. "No puedo descartar que, si nos enfrentamos a precios de la energía tan elevados como estos, tengamos que adentrarnos en un territorio de política monetaria ligeramente restrictiva", dijo. No obstante, restó importancia a algunas preocupaciones sobre los efectos de segunda ronda de la inflación, argumentando que el mercado laboral se encontraba en una situación mucho más débil que en 2022, cuando una inflación impulsada por los precios de la energía avivó las crecientes demandas salariales, lo que condujo a una espiral de salarios y precios. También señaló que no se observaban efectos de segunda ronda significativos en los datos. Por el momento, el BCE debía mantener su enfoque de tomar decisiones reunión tras reunión, añadió Nagel. Esto significa que la política monetaria debe situarse en algún punto entre la "ambigüedad constructiva" —o vaguedad intencionada— y el establecimiento de "orientaciones prospectivas" o la asunción de compromisos explícitos sobre futuras medidas de política monetaria, dijo Nagel.

item.title: South African rand muted ahead of inflation data, expected rate hike
item.description: The South African rand was muted in early trade on Wednesday as investors awaited inflation data and a monetary policy decision later in the day, with the central bank widely expected to raise interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The South African rand was muted in early trade on Wednesday as investors awaited inflation data and a monetary policy decision later in the day, with the central bank widely expected to raise interest rates. At 0616 GMT, the rand traded at 16.2125 against the dollar , down about 0.2% from its previous close. Statistics South Africa is due to publish August inflation data (ZACPIY=ECI) at 0800 GMT. Analysts polled by Reuters expect annual inflation to accelerate to 4.5%, from 4.3% in July. However, Nedbank economists forecast headline consumer inflation would remain unchanged at 4.3%, citing lower transport costs due to a decline in fuel prices. As a net fuel importer, South Africa is heavily exposed to swings in global energy prices. Later in the day, the South African Reserve Bank will announce its policy decision, with the central bank widely expected to deliver a 25-basis-point rate hike after leaving rates unchanged at its previous meeting. "Inflation looks set to remain above the target for some time, our forecast suggests another 10 months. This is long enough to undermine policy credibility and unsettle inflation expectations," Nedbank economists said in a note. "The rand's impressive resilience will depend on the SARB hiking, or it will reverse," ETM Analytics said in a note, adding there was plenty of room for disappointment should the central bank not raise rates. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was steady in early deals, with the yield at 8.585%.

item.title: Taiwán y los derechos humanos son "líneas rojas" para China para la reunión entre Trump y Xi
item.description: Taiwán y los derechos humanos son "líneas rojas" para China que no se pueden traspasar, advirtió el miércoles el embajador de ese país en EEUU, adoptando un tono firme de cara a la cumbre entre los líderes que se celebrará esta semana en Washington.
item.dc:creator: Liz Lee, Yimou Lee
item.content:encoded: Taiwán y los derechos humanos son "líneas rojas" para China que no se pueden traspasar, advirtió el miércoles el embajador de ese país en EEUU, adoptando un tono firme de cara a la cumbre entre los líderes que se celebrará esta semana en Washington. El presidente chino, Xi Jinping, visitará Washington para una cumbre con el presidente Donald Trump, en un momento en que ambas partes buscan aportar estabilidad a unas relaciones ensombrecidas por disputas que abarcan desde el comercio hasta Taiwán. En un artículo publicado en el Diario del Pueblo, órgano oficial del Partido Comunista en el poder, el mismo día en que Xi tiene previsto partir, el embajador Xie Feng dijo que la gestión de las diferencias depende de la buena fe, y que EEUU debería dejar de "inventar pretextos" como la seguridad nacional, los desequilibrios económicos y el trabajo forzoso para intentar contener a China. Añadió que, cuando China y EEUU cooperan, ambas partes se benefician, pero cuando se enfrentan, ambas salen perjudicadas. "No se pueden violar los intereses de China en materia de soberanía, seguridad y desarrollo, y no se pueden cuestionar las cuatro líneas rojas: Taiwán, la democracia y los derechos humanos, las vías y los sistemas de desarrollo, y los derechos al desarrollo", afirmó Xie. "China está comprometida con el desarrollo pacífico y espera que EEUU también avance en esa dirección". China reclama Taiwán, gobernado democráticamente, como parte de su territorio, a pesar de las objeciones del Gobierno de Taipéi. TENSIONES EN TAIWÁN Estados Unidos es el principal proveedor de armas y el principal apoyo internacional de Taiwán, y China ha exigido en repetidas ocasiones que se ponga fin a la venta de armas a Taiwán. Tras una cumbre celebrada en mayo en Pekín con Xi, Trump dijo que tenía en suspenso un nuevo paquete de armas, por valor de unos 14.000 millones de dólares, y lo describió como una "baza muy buena para la negociación". Un alto cargo de seguridad taiwanés dijo a los periodistas que Pekín considera cualquier retraso en las transferencias de armas de EEUU como una forma directa de frenar el refuerzo militar de Taiwán, lo que da a China más margen para aumentar la presión en torno a Taiwán, Japón y Filipinas. China podría recurrir a un paquete de incentivos, como la compra de productos estadounidenses o gestos respecto a las tensiones en Oriente Medio, para convencer a Trump de que una reducción de los compromisos militares de EEUU en la región podría granjearle una mayor cooperación por parte de Pekín, dijo el representante, que habló bajo condición de anonimato. Las fuerzas armadas chinas han aumentado significativamente el número de buques de la Armada, de la guardia costera y de investigación en torno a Taiwán, en los mares del Sur y de China Oriental, y están recopilando datos sobre elementos como los cables submarinos que podrían resultar útiles en caso de guerra, señaló el funcionario. El Ministerio de Defensa chino no respondió a las solicitudes de comentarios. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China reiteró su "firme oposición" a la venta de armas por parte de EEUU, afirmando que la cuestión de Taiwán era su "interés fundamental entre los intereses fundamentales" y la base política de las relaciones entre China y EEUU. China nunca ha renunciado al uso de la fuerza para someter a Taiwán a su control, aunque afirma que preferiría una "reunificación pacífica". En Pekín, un portavoz de la Oficina de Asuntos de Taiwán dijo que era Taiwán quien estaba intensificando "deliberadamente" la confrontación. "Las maquinaciones en favor de la independencia son las principales responsables de destruir la paz y la estabilidad en el estrecho de Taiwán y de socavar el 'statu quo'", dijo la portavoz Zhu Fenglian.

item.title: EEUU financiará proyectos mineros y energéticos en Argentina con 7.000 millones, según documento
item.description: El Banco de Exportación e Importación de Estados Unidos tiene previsto financiar proyectos relacionados con minerales críticos y energía en Argentina por un valor de hasta 7.000 millones de dólares, según un documento al que tuvo acceso Reuters, como parte de una iniciativa para profundizar la cooperación económica entre Washington y Buenos Aires.
item.dc:creator: Ernest Scheyder, Lucinda Elliott
item.content:encoded: El Banco de Exportación e Importación de Estados Unidos tiene previsto financiar proyectos relacionados con minerales críticos y energía en Argentina por un valor de hasta 7.000 millones de dólares, según un documento al que tuvo acceso Reuters, como parte de una iniciativa para profundizar la cooperación económica entre Washington y Buenos Aires. La financiación forma parte de un paquete que se anunciará el miércoles en Nueva York durante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas, según una fuente familiarizada con el asunto, en un momento en que Estados Unidos busca un mayor acceso a la energía y a los minerales críticos del hemisferio occidental. Bajo el mandato del presidente argentino Javier Milei, estrecho aliado del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump, las relaciones entre Washington y Buenos Aires han mejorado gracias a una mayor convergencia en materia de política económica. La relación se ha visto reforzada por el respaldo de EEUU a las reformas orientadas al mercado de Milei y por un acuerdo preferencial de comercio e inversión anunciado en febrero que incluía la cooperación en materia de minerales críticos. El Congreso argentino aún no ha ratificado el acuerdo bilateral. La Presidencia argentina no respondió de inmediato a la solicitud de comentarios. Argentina cuenta con grandes yacimientos de litio, petróleo de esquisto y otras materias primas. Los fondos estadounidenses permitirán a las empresas que operan en el país sudamericano recibir préstamos para adquirir equipos de fabricantes estadounidenses, entre otros usos, durante los próximos dos años. Argentina, Chile y Bolivia forman el denominado "triángulo del litio", donde se concentran los mayores suministros mundiales de este metal blanco utilizado en electrónica, vehículos eléctricos y otras tecnologías clave. Entre las principales empresas de materias primas que ya operan en Argentina se encuentran Rio Tinto (RIO.AX) , que extrae litio para su uso en baterías; BHP (BHP.AX) , que está desarrollando un proyecto de cobre; y Chevron (CVX.N) , que cuenta con un gran proyecto de petróleo y gas de esquisto. El Gobierno de Milei, que se enfrenta a unas elecciones presidenciales en 2027, ha promovido un régimen de incentivos para grandes inversiones conocido como RIGI, como piedra angular de los esfuerzos por atraer capital extranjero a sectores estratégicos como la energía, la minería y las infraestructuras. La italiana Eni (ENI.MI) y la estatal argentina YPF (YPFDm.BA) presentaron el mes pasado una solicitud conjunta en el marco del RIGI para su proyecto de gas natural licuado, valorado en 51.000 millones de dólares. Luis Lucero, ministro de Minería de Argentina, dijo este año a Reuters que su país podría llegar a exportar 580.000 toneladas métricas de litio y 1.641.000 toneladas métricas de cobre al año para 2036, lo que supondría un volumen cinco veces superior al de 2025.

item.content:encoded: Britain's Co-op Group posted a bigger first-half loss on Wednesday as spending on promotions and store improvements weighed on profitability. The member-owned retailer, which runs more than 2,500 food stores and provides funeral, insurance and legal services, posted a £45 million ($59.89 million) underlying operating loss for the six months ended July 4, compared with a £32 million loss a year earlier.
